tip: Many adjectives ending in -co add an h in the plural to keep the hard c sound: stanco becomes stanchi.
Origin uses di: Di dove sei? = where are you from, literally of where are you.
Cambiare idea means to change one's mind, with no possessive word added: cambiato idea.
Aspettare already means to wait for, so there is no separate word for for: aspettato un'ora.
A negative informal command is non plus the infinitive: non mangiare = don't eat.
The noi present form also means let's: mangiamo = let's eat.
Chi means whoever and always takes a singular verb: chi studia = those who study.
Prendere has the irregular past participle preso, not prenduto.
Reflexive verbs form the past with essere, so the participle agrees: si è sentito.
Clock times use a plus le: arrivo alle otto = I arrive at eight o'clock.
Fino a means up to or until: conto fino a dieci = I count to ten.
Tutto agrees and keeps the article after it: tutta la sera = the whole evening.
Bisognava che expresses necessity and takes the imperfect subjunctive: bisognava che studiassimo.
Qualunque, meaning whatever or any, triggers the subjunctive: qualunque cosa dicesse, not diceva.
A past main verb pulls the subjunctive into the imperfect: pensavo che tu parlassi, not parli.
Grocery shopping is fare la spesa, built on fare, not comprare.

target: Fermati, hai dimenticato il tuo cappotto!
tip: In an informal command the reflexive pronoun attaches to the end: ferma plus ti gives fermati.

target: Il mese scorso ha cambiato lavoro.
tip: Scorso means last in the sense of just past: il mese scorso = last month.

target: Abbiamo letto le recensioni del ristorante.
tip: Leggere has the irregular past participle letto.

target: I bambini hanno rotto la lampada.
tip: Rompere has the irregular past participle rotto.

target: Ha preso la macchina di sua madre.
tip: Possession is shown with di: la macchina di sua madre = his mother's car.
Da plus l' contracts to dall': dall'ufficio = from the office.
Object pronouns attach to the end of an infinitive: chiamare plus ti gives chiamarti.
Quello shortens to quel before a masculine noun starting with a consonant: quel libro.

english: I wish I spoke five languages!
tip: Magari plus the past subjunctive expresses a wish: magari parlassi = I wish I spoke.
Svegliarsi is reflexive, so it needs mi: mi sveglio = I wake up, literally I wake myself.

english: Did you see the movie yesterday?
tip: Vedere has the irregular past participle visto.

english: She came to visit me yesterday.
tip: To visit a person use andare or venire a trovare; visitare is for places: venuta a trovarmi.

english: There are only a few seats left.
tip: Rimanere takes essere, so its participle agrees with the subject: pochi posti sono rimasti = few seats are left.

english: When I woke up, it was snowing.
tip: Passato prossimo (mi sono svegliato) for event + imperfetto (nevicava) for weather.
